stemMd: Let $P=\{1,2,3\}$ and $Q=\{2,4\}$. How many ordered pairs are in $P\times Q$?
explanationMd: Each of the three first coordinates can pair with either of two second coordinates. The product rule gives $3\times2=6$, regardless of overlap between the sets.

distractorRationale.a: Counts the shared element rather than ordered pairs.
